title: GET /api/Machine/{id} throws JSON serialization exception (object cycle)
body:
## Problem

`GET /api/Machine/{id}` throws a `System.Text.Json.JsonException` due to a
detected object cycle when serializing the response.

## Error

System.Text.Json.JsonException: A possible object cycle was detected. This
can either be due to a cycle or if the object depth is larger than the
maximum allowed depth of 32.
Path: $.Location.Machines.Location.Machines.Location.Machines...

## Root cause (likely)

`GetMachine(int id)` in `MachineController.cs` returns the raw `Machine`
entity (including `.Include(m => m.Location)`) directly, instead of mapping
it to a DTO like `MachineResponse`:

    var machine = await _context.Machines
        .Include(m => m.Location)
        .FirstOrDefaultAsync(m => m.MachineId == id);

    return machine;

Since `Machine.Location` likely has a navigation collection back to
`Location.Machines`, the serializer enters a cycle:
`Machine → Location → Machines → Location → Machines → ...`

This differs from `GetMachines()` (the list endpoint), which maps each
machine to a `MachineResponse` DTO and does not exhibit this issue.

## Impact

- `GET /api/Machine/{id}` is broken for all roles (Technician and Manager
  both affected — this is not an authorization issue).
- Discovered incidentally during #7 checkpoint verification while
  confirming a Manager-created test machine (`machineId: 2`) after a PUT
  update. The list endpoint (`GET /api/Machine`) was used as a workaround
  to confirm state instead.

## Suggested fix

Map the result to `MachineResponse` (or an equivalent DTO) in
`GetMachine(int id)`, consistent with `GetMachines()`, so the response
does not include the cyclical `Location.Machines` navigation.

## Not blocking #7

This does not block Checkpoint 1 (#7), since the E2E verification only
relied on the list endpoint (`GET /api/Machine`), which functions
correctly. Flagged here for follow-up during Milestone 6+ work.

title: Seeded Manager account has invalid password hash
body:
## Problem

The seeded Manager account currently uses `PasswordHash = "placeholder-hash"` in `DbSeeder.cs`.

This is not a valid BCrypt password hash. When attempting to log in as the seeded Manager through the normal login flow, authentication fails with:

`BCrypt.Net.SaltParseException: Invalid salt version`

This prevents us from completing an end-to-end verification of the Manager authentication and Manager-only Machine API operations.

## Expected

The seeded Manager account should have a valid BCrypt password hash so that the account can authenticate through the normal login flow.

## Current verification

The issue was verified by:

* Inspecting `DbSeeder.cs` and confirming the Manager is seeded with `"placeholder-hash"`.
* Inspecting the database and confirming the same value is stored for the Manager user.
* Attempting to log in as the Manager through the application.
* Confirming that BCrypt throws `SaltParseException: Invalid salt version`.

## Scope

This is a seed/authentication issue. It is separate from the Manager authorization and CRUD functionality tracked in #30 and #31.

Fix the seeded Manager credentials, then continue with end-to-end verification of the Manager flow.
